name: Witness
tagline: AI notices, AI labels and machine-readable marking for Article 50 of the EU AI Act, for any web app and the Vercel AI SDK.
seoTitle: Witness – AI Act Article 50 transparency kit: chatbot notice, AI labels, image and text marking
description:
Since 2 August 2026, Article 50 of the EU AI Act asks for transparency around AI: people must know when they are talking to a chatbot, generated content must be marked in a machine-readable way, and deepfakes and AI text on matters of public interest must be disclosed. Witness gives you the building blocks for that in one small package.

A chatbot notice and an AI label as web components and React components, in English, German, French and Italian. IPTC/XMP marking written straight into image, audio and video files (PNG, JPEG, WebP, MP3, WAV, MP4, MOV, M4A), an invisible watermark for generated text, schema.org and meta tags for pages, and middleware for the Vercel AI SDK that marks text and images as the model produces them. Witness is a tool, not legal advice: it helps you implement the duties, it does not confirm compliance.

faq.q: Does Witness make my site compliant with the AI Act?
faq.a: No tool can promise that. Witness implements the transparency measures Article 50 describes: the chatbot notice, visible labels and machine-readable marking. Whether they are enough for your case depends on your role, your system and the guidance that is still being finalised. The docs summarise the duties with sources; for a binding answer ask a lawyer.

The chatbot notice of Article 50(1), machine-readable marking of generated images and text for 50(2), and visible labels for deepfakes and AI text on matters of public interest under 50(4). Emotion recognition and biometric categorisation (50(3)) get notice wording, but the duty itself lies in how you inform people. Audio and video files get the same machine-readable XMP marking as images; a watermark inside the sound or picture itself is out of scope.

faq.q: Does Witness sign images with C2PA?
faq.a: No. Witness writes IPTC/XMP metadata, which needs no certificate. Images that already carry a C2PA manifest from the generator are left unchanged so the signature stays valid.

faq.q: Can the text watermark be removed?
faq.a: Yes, on purpose it can. It survives normal copy and paste but not someone who strips it. Treat it as one layer next to the visible label and the metadata, not as proof.

faq.q: Does it work without React or the Vercel AI SDK?
faq.a: Yes. The notice and label are standard web components, and image and text marking are plain functions that also run in the browser. The React package and the AI SDK middleware are optional.
